claim: Silencing neurotransmission in DMHLepR neurons in adult mice increases body weight and adiposity.
source: Using a viral approach, we show that silencing neurotransmission in DMHLepR neurons in adult mice not only increases body weight and adiposity but also phase-advances diurnal rhythms of feeding and metabolism into the light cycle and abolishes the normal increase in dark-cycle locomotor activity characteristic of nocturnal rodents.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 1.

claim: Synchrony between behavior and environmental rhythms enables animals to predict food availability and optimize metabolism in anticipation of daily periods of fasting and feeding.
source: Synchrony between behavior and environmental rhythms enables animals to predict food availability and optimize metabolism in anticipation of daily periods of fasting and feeding (Saper et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction with a citation.

claim: Leptin-induced pSTAT3 is a marker of LepR signal transduction.
source: First, the specificity of GFP:TeTx expression in DMHLepR neurons was confirmed by establishing that leptin-induced pSTAT3, a marker of LepR signal transduction, colocalizes with virally transduced cells following systemic leptin injection (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: All procedures were performed in accordance with the National Institutes of Health Guide for the Care and Use of Laboratory Animals.
source: All procedures were performed in accordance with the National Institutes of Health Guide for the Care and Use of Laboratory Animals and were approved by the Animal Care Committee at the University of Washington.
evidence: This describes the ethical compliance of the study.

claim: All procedures were approved by the Animal Care Committee at the University of Washington.
source: All procedures were performed in accordance with the National Institutes of Health Guide for the Care and Use of Laboratory Animals and were approved by the Animal Care Committee at the University of Washington.
evidence: This describes the ethical compliance of the study.

claim: Following stereotaxic surgery, all studied animals were individually housed with ad lib access to standard chow diet in a temperature- and humidity-controlled facility with 14:10 light–dark cycles.
source: Following stereotaxic surgery, all studied animals were individually housed with ad lib access to standard chow diet (LabDiet 5053) in a temperature- and humidity-controlled facility with 14:10 light–dark cycles.
evidence: This describes the experimental conditions.

claim: Adult LeprIRES-Cre/+ (LepR-Cre) mice or Cre-littermate controls were used for all experiments.
source: Adult LeprIRES-Cre/+ (LepR-Cre) mice (Jackson Laboratory no. 008320) or Cre-littermate controls were used for all experiments, as described below.
evidence: This describes the experimental subjects.

claim: The viral vector AAV1-CBA-DIO-GFP:TeTx was generated and validated as described.
source: The viral vector AAV1-CBA-DIO-GFP:TeTx (TeTx) was generated and validated as described (Han et al., 2015; Chen et al., 2018) and generously provided by Dr. Richard Palmiter and Dr. Larry Zweifel (University of Washington, Seattle, WA).
evidence: This describes the source and validation of the viral vector with citations.

claim: AAV was delivered using a Hamilton syringe with a 33-gauge needle at a rate of 50 nL/min.
source: AAV) was delivered using a Hamilton syringe with a 33-gauge needle at a rate of 50 nL/min (Micro4 controller), followed by a 5 min wait at the injection site and a 1 min wait 0.05 mm dorsal to the injection site before needle withdrawal.
evidence: This describes the experimental method.

claim: Animals received a perioperative subcutaneous injection of buprenorphine hydrochloride (0.05 mg/kg).
source: Animals received a perioperative subcutaneous injection of buprenorphine hydrochloride (0.05 mg/kg; Reckitt Benckiser, Richmond, VA).
evidence: This describes the experimental procedure.

claim: Viral expression was verified post hoc in all animals.
source: Viral expression was verified post hoc in all animals, and any data from animals in which the virus expressed outside the targeted area were excluded from the analysis.
evidence: This describes the quality control procedure.

claim: Any data from animals in which the virus expressed outside the targeted area were excluded from the analysis.
source: Viral expression was verified post hoc in all animals, and any data from animals in which the virus expressed outside the targeted area were excluded from the analysis.
evidence: This describes the quality control procedure.

claim: Measurements of body lean and fat mass were determined in live, conscious mice by use of quantitative magnetic resonance spectroscopy (QMR).
source: Measurements of body lean and fat mass were determined in live, conscious mice by use of quantitative magnetic resonance spectroscopy (QMR; EchoMRI 3-in-1; Echo MRI, Houston, TX) by the University of Washington Nutrition Obesity Research Center Energy Balance Core.
evidence: This describes the experimental method.

claim: Ad lib fed mice were injected intraperitoneally with leptin (5 mg/kg) and perfused 90 min later to validate the ability of leptin to elicit pSTAT3 signaling in DMHLepR neurons.
source: To validate the ability of leptin to elicit pSTAT3 signaling in DMHLepR neurons, ad lib fed mice were injected intraperitoneally with leptin (5 mg/kg; Dr. Parlow; National Hormone Peptide Program) and perfused 90 min later, as described below.
evidence: This describes the experimental method.

claim: Mice were fasted for 24 hr from ZT2 to ZT2' to assess the ability of leptin to suppress the compensatory hyperphagia that normally follows a prolonged fast.
source: To assess the ability of leptin to suppress the compensatory hyperphagia that normally follows a prolonged fast, mice were fasted for 24 hr from ZT2 to ZT2'.
evidence: This describes the experimental method.

claim: Leptin (3 mg/kg) or vehicle control (PBS, pH 7.9) was injected intraperitoneally in mice 15 min before preweighed food was placed back in the cage.
source: On the second day, leptin (3 mg/kg) or vehicle control (PBS, pH 7.9) was injected intraperitoneally in mice 15 min before preweighed food was placed back in the cage, and intake was monitored for the following 24 hr.
evidence: This describes the experimental method.

claim: Prior to surgery, mice were acclimated to calorimetry cages for at least 7 days.
source: Prior to surgery, mice were acclimated to calorimetry cages for at least 7 days, during which time baseline pre-intervention calorimetry values were obtained for each subject.
evidence: This describes the experimental method.

claim: The first 12–16 hr of data (including the first dark cycle) were omitted from all analyses, except for the TRF experiment where continuous intake measurements were required.
source: To account for potential confounding effects of stress resulting from rehousing into calorimetry during study, the first 12–16 hr of data (including the first dark cycle) were omitted from all analyses, except for the TRF experiment where continuous intake measurements were required.
evidence: This describes the data analysis procedure.

claim: Energy expenditure measurements were obtained by a computer-controlled indirect calorimeter system (Promethion, Sable Systems).
source: Energy expenditure measurements were obtained by a computer-controlled indirect calorimeter system (Promethion, Sable Systems, Las Vegas NV) with support from the Energy Balance Core of the NORC at the University of Washington, as previously described (Kaiyala et al., 2015).
evidence: This describes the experimental method with a citation.

claim: Oxygen consumption (VO2) and carbon dioxide production (VCO2) were sequentially measured for each mouse for 30 s at 5 min intervals.
source: Oxygen consumption (VO2) and carbon dioxide production (VCO2) were sequentially measured for each mouse for 30 s at 5 min intervals, and food and water intakes were measured continuously while mice were housed in a temperature- and humidity-controlled cabinet (Caron Products and Services, Marietta, OH).
evidence: This describes the experimental method.

claim: Food and water intakes were measured continuously while mice were housed in a temperature- and humidity-controlled cabinet.
source: Oxygen consumption (VO2) and carbon dioxide production (VCO2) were sequentially measured for each mouse for 30 s at 5 min intervals, and food and water intakes were measured continuously while mice were housed in a temperature- and humidity-controlled cabinet (Caron Products and Services, Marietta, OH).
evidence: This describes the experimental method.

claim: Ambulatory activity was determined simultaneously and beam breaks in the y-axis were scored as an activity count.
source: Ambulatory activity was determined simultaneously and beam breaks in the y-axis were scored as an activity count, and a tally was recorded every 3 min.
evidence: This describes the experimental method.

claim: Data acquisition and instrument control were coordinated by MetaScreen v2.3.15.11.
source: Data acquisition and instrument control were coordinated by MetaScreen v2.3.15.11, and raw data were processed and binned into 2-hr increments using ExpeData v1.9.14 (Sable Systems, Las Vegas, NV) using an analysis script documenting all aspects of data transformation.
evidence: This describes the data acquisition method.

claim: Raw data were processed and binned into 2-hr increments using ExpeData v1.9.14.
source: Data acquisition and instrument control were coordinated by MetaScreen v2.3.15.11, and raw data were processed and binned into 2-hr increments using ExpeData v1.9.14 (Sable Systems, Las Vegas, NV) using an analysis script documenting all aspects of data transformation.
evidence: This describes the data processing method.

claim: One day before TRF, animals were placed into clean bedding and fasted for 24 hr from ZT14 (on day 1) to ZT14' (on day 0) before TRF began.
source: To eliminate the initial effects of varying fed status of animals, 1 day before TRF, animals were placed into clean bedding and fasted for 24 hr from ZT14 (on day 1) to ZT14' (on day 0) before TRF began.
evidence: This describes the experimental method.

claim: Food was removed each morning at the start of the light cycle (ZT0) and the bedding inspected to ensure no residual food debris remained accessible.
source: Food was removed each morning at the start of the light cycle (ZT0) and the bedding inspected to ensure no residual food debris remained accessible.
evidence: This describes the experimental method.

claim: Food was returned at the start of the dark cycle (ZT14) each day.
source: Food was returned at the start of the dark cycle (ZT14) each day.
evidence: This describes the experimental method.

claim: Body weight was measured at both ZT0 and ZT14 daily during TRF.
source: Body weight was also measured at both ZT0 and ZT14 daily.
evidence: This describes the experimental method.

claim: Animals were maintained on TRF for a total of 5 days in home cages, then subjected to indirect calorimetry for four additional days of TRF before returning to ad lib feeding for the remaining 3 days of study.
source: Animals were maintained on TRF for a total of 5 days in home cages, then subjected to indirect calorimetry for four additional days of TRF before returning to ad lib feeding for the remaining 3 days of study (Figure 4A).
evidence: This describes the experimental design shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Animals were terminally anesthetized with ketamine:xylazine and transcardially perfused with PBS followed by 4% paraformaldehyde in 0.1 mol/L PBS for brain immunohistochemical analyses.
source: For brain immunohistochemical analyses, animals were terminally anesthetized with ketamine:xylazine and transcardially perfused with PBS followed by 4% paraformaldehyde in 0.1 mol/L PBS.
evidence: This describes the experimental method.

claim: Brains were removed and postfixed overnight, then transferred into 30% sucrose overnight or until brains sunk in solution.
source: Brains were removed and postfixed overnight, then transferred into 30% sucrose overnight or until brains sunk in solution.
evidence: This describes the experimental method.

claim: Brains were sectioned on a freezing-stage microtome to obtain 30 μm coronal sections in four series.
source: Brains were subsequently sectioned on a freezing-stage microtome (Leica) to obtain 30 μm coronal sections in four series.
evidence: This describes the experimental method.

claim: Tail blood for plasma hormonal measurement was collected at indicated times.
source: Tail blood for plasma hormonal measurement was collected at indicated times.
evidence: This describes the experimental method.

claim: Blood was collected via EDTA-coated capillary tubes and centrifuged at 4°C (7000 rpm, 4 min), and plasma was subsequently removed and stored at −80°C for subsequent assay.
source: Blood was collected via EDTA-coated capillary tubes and centrifuged at 4°C (7000 rpm, 4 min), and plasma was subsequently removed and stored at −80°C for subsequent assay.
evidence: This describes the experimental method.

claim: Plasma leptin was determined by ELISA.
source: Plasma leptin (Crystal Chem, Elk Grove Village, IL; #90030) and plasma insulin (Crystal Chem; #90080) were determined by ELISA.
evidence: This describes the experimental method.

claim: Plasma insulin was determined by ELISA.
source: Plasma leptin (Crystal Chem, Elk Grove Village, IL; #90030) and plasma insulin (Crystal Chem; #90080) were determined by ELISA.
evidence: This describes the experimental method.

claim: Prior to analysis, all data were tested for normality by Shapiro–Wilk normality test.
source: Prior to analysis, all data were tested for normality by Shapiro–Wilk normality test.
evidence: This describes the statistical analysis method.

claim: P values for unpaired comparisons were calculated by two-tailed Student's t test.
source: P values for unpaired comparisons were calculated by two-tailed Student's t test.
evidence: This describes the statistical analysis method.

claim: Time course comparisons between groups were analyzed using a two-way repeated-measures ANOVA with main effects of treatment (control vs. TeTx) and time.
source: Time course comparisons between groups were analyzed using a two-way repeated-measures ANOVA with main effects of treatment (control vs. TeTx) and time.
evidence: This describes the statistical analysis method.

claim: All post hoc comparisons were determined using Sidak's correction for multiple comparisons.
source: All post hoc comparisons were determined using Sidak's correction for multiple comparisons.
evidence: This describes the statistical analysis method.

claim: All statistical tests indicated were performed using Prism (version 7.4; GraphPad, San Diego, CA) software.
source: All statistical tests indicated were performed using Prism (version 7.4; GraphPad, San Diego, CA) software.
evidence: This describes the statistical analysis software.
